messages:
alice: seeing weird p95 jumps between gnode-f[2-7] during peak batching window (12:00-12:06). p95 ~200ms -> ~900ms, throughput steady but a bunch of RDMA rx_dropped++ on mlx5 counters. not MTU related AFAICT.
ben: can you paste the mlx5/ethtool counters?
alice: here, grabbed from node gnode-f2 a few mins ago:
```
mlx5_core: rx_dropped: 1245
mlx5_core: rx_crc_errors: 0
eth0: rx_no_buffer: 0
eth0: rx_missed_errors: 890
rx_packets: 12834567
tx_packets: 12834210
```
carla: tor queues on rack-f showed qlen spikes at same time, saw interrupts pile up on the TOR CPU0. may be microbursting optics.
dan: any recent BGP or ECMP changes? ECMP churn could shift flows across different paths and trigger path asymmetry.
alice: not aware of config changes. infra-bot: "driver-rollout/mlx5-upgrade" completed on gnode-f4 at 11:58 (canary), but rollout paused at 12:03 due to alerts.
erin: ethtool -S from gnode-f2 after spike:
```
rx_packets: 12834567
rx_errors: 0
rx_dropped: 1245
rx_mbuf_alloc_failed: 720
```
maya: rx_mbuf_alloc_failed + missed_errors suggests NIC ring buffer pressure + skb allocation stalls. might be interrupt moderation + coalescing interacting poorly with kernel offloads under bursts.
raj: temporary mitigation: reduce max batch window on affected pools by 30% and spread batches over 15s to smooth out demand. less ideal but buys time.
ben: agree. also let's toggle RSS/flow steering offload (mlx5) on a test node and repro. that has fixed similar microburst pathing before.
carla: optics look marginal on f5 link pairs - SFP Tx power low on one side, will probe. low optical power + bursty packets can cause packet losses that show as rx_dropped downstream.
dan: also double-check if any k8s CNI upgrades touched tx-checksum offload flags. CNI offloads + SR-IOV config can change flow distribution.
alice: running pcap on one flow now, capturing 30s during a controlled small-batch run. posting snippet:
```
12:02:15.123 IP gnode-f2 > gnode-f4: seq 12345 ack 67890 win 65535 len 1400
12:02:15.124 IP retransmission  seq 12345 len 1400
12:02:15.125 IP gnode-f2 > gnode-f4: seq 12345 len 64
```
maya: retransmits but no CRCs -> points to drops under congestion, not link-level corruption. increase ring size, tune NAPI weight on test node.
ben: I'd also try disabling LRO/GRO on test nodes; sometimes large coalesced frames hide microbursts until kernel processes them.
erin: quick cost note: for the affected tenants we estimate ~+18% GPU runtime due to retries and slower batches during the 6 minute window yesterday. we should include that when discussing rollback windows.
raj: ops plan: 1) small traffic-shaping rollout (limit batch concurrency) now, 2) test disabling RSS offload on gnode-f2/f3, 3) firmware + SFP swap on f5-f6 if optics confirm, 4) if confirmed, schedule staged MLX5 firmware bump and kernel param change (net.core.rmem_max, ring buffer).
alice: doing step 1 now. collecting pcaps and ethtool/mlx5 dumps for the incident ticket. assigning to @maya and @carla for hardware checks.
infra-bot: Created incident INC-2026-0423-07: "east-west microbursting causing RDMA rx_dropped during peak batch window". priority P2.
ben: timeline estimate: small-shape + tests by EOD. firmware/SFP swap early next maintenance window if hardware confirms.
carla: FYI swapped one SFP on f5, immediate mitigation on that pair, p95 back to ~220ms for 5m. looks promising.
alice: great — will leave shaping on until we finish validation. will post pcaps to ticket.
maya: follow-up: plan kernel tuning doc and add as runbook item for batch window ops.
raj: thanks all. action items in INC-2026-0423-07.
